name: Charli xcx
label: Atlantic
lede: She writes a No. 1 for someone else, spends two years making pop her own label doesn't know what to do with, then gives a whole summer her name.

eras.title: Myspace demos, and a hit she gave away
eras.text: A teenager posts demos on Myspace, lands on the bill at illegal East London raves, and by 2012 has written a global hit for someone else. Her own debut arrives in 2013 to better reviews than sales.

years.h: At fifteen she's on Myspace and on the bill at illegal warehouse raves
years.p: Charlotte Aitchison posts demos as Charli XCX and gets booked by a promoter who runs East London warehouse parties. Her parents come to some of the shows.
years.xp:
The name came from her MSN Messenger handle. In late 2008 she put out two singles on Orgy Music, "!Franchesckaar!" and the double A-side "Emelline"/"Art Bitch". She has since called that era "fucking terrible Myspace music".

She moved to London to study fine art at UCL's Slade School and dropped out in her second year. She had signed to Asylum Records in 2010, and has described the years after as "lost".

years.h: Pitchfork tags "Stay Away" and "Nuclear Seasons" Best New Track
years.p: Both singles get the tag, and "Stay Away" lands on Pitchfork's Best Tracks of 2011 list.
years.xp: Early in 2011 she was also featured on [[Alex Metric|286021ca-b6eb-42eb-80b9-502f14e16ce6]]'s single "End of the World". Her label years in Los Angeles were slow until she started working with the producer Ariel Rechtshaid, after which, she says, things started to come together.

years.src: Wikipedia: I Love It (Icona Pop song) · Wikipedia: Charli XCX
years.h: She writes "I Love It", decides it isn't hers, and Icona Pop take it to No. 1
years.p: Charli xcx and Patrik Berger write the song and she decides it doesn't fit her own sound. [[Icona Pop|c5f259d0-abd8-418e-81ee-3965fd4e4e9a]] release it in Sweden on May 9, 2012, and it reaches No. 1 in the UK in June 2013.
years.xp:
Berger sent her two beats and she wrote a song over each; one became "I Love It". Icona Pop's Aino Jawo connected with it, and the duo asked the producer Style of Eye for a rougher version, telling him they wanted "the punkiness" and "the 'fuck it' feeling".

An appearance on an episode of Girls in January 2013 sent downloads up, and in the US it peaked at No. 7 on the Hot 100. The vocal on the released track is the demo vocal Icona Pop reworked.

years.h: True Romance debuts at No. 85 in the UK
years.p: Moody 80s synth-pop and girl-group sass, with Rechtshaid producing. It is her debut on Asylum.
years.xp:
Other producers include Justin Raisen, Blood Diamonds and Berger. Five singles came off it, from "Stay Away" in 2011 to "What I Like" in April 2013. Pitchfork gave it 8.3, with Marc Hogan writing that she pulled from 80s synth-pop, turn-of-the-millennium girl groups and current producers.

Before it she had put out two mixtapes: Heartbreaks and Earthquakes in June 2012, and Super Ultra in November, which was distributed only through her website.

eras.title: Two hooks and a second album
eras.text: One hook goes to a rapper and one to a teen-cancer movie, and radio starts calling. Her second album leans into it, and then she starts asking what else she could sound like.

years.src: Wikipedia: Fancy (Iggy Azalea song) · Wikipedia: Sucker (Charli XCX album)
years.h: Her hook on "Fancy" sits at No. 1 for seven weeks
years.p: [[Iggy Azalea|3a052c99-8c18-484a-8beb-9873b4fb3106]]'s single tops the Hot 100 for seven consecutive weeks, while Azalea also holds No. 2 with "Problem".
years.xp:
Wikipedia notes Azalea was the first act since the Beatles to have her first two Hot 100 entries at Nos. 1 and 2 at the same time. "Fancy" was named Billboard's Song of the Summer for 2014.

In June that year Charli's own "Boom Clap", made for the film The Fault in Our Stars, reached No. 8 on the Hot 100 and No. 6 in the UK.

years.h: Sucker debuts at No. 28 on the Billboard 200
years.p: It is her first Billboard 200 entry, and it opens at No. 15 in the UK. Producers include Patrik Berger, Greg Kurstin, Stargate and Rostam Batmanglij.
years.xp:
Singles: "Boom Clap", "Break the Rules", "Doing It" with [[Rita Ora|c9dd033c-0270-463c-b3ec-f4b7712486fe]], which reached No. 8 in the UK, and "Famous". Pitchfork gave it 7.6, and Wikipedia records Rolling Stone naming it the best pop album of 2014.

She opened for [[Katy Perry|122d63fc-8671-43e4-9752-34e846d62a9c]]'s Prismatic World Tour in early 2015.

eras.title: Vroom Vroom, and the PC Music years
eras.text: Charli hands the controls to SOPHIE and A. G. Cook and spends two years making some of the strangest pop on a major label's books. The label doesn't always love it, and critics come round.

years.h: SOPHIE produces Vroom Vroom and Charli starts her own label
years.p: She announces Vroom Vroom Recordings on February 23 and the EP lands three days later. A. G. Cook co-writes "Paradise" with [[Hannah Diamond|76130c0b-b177-434f-893f-46c8d819548d]].
years.xp:
She premiered the title track on Beats 1 on October 20, 2015 as the lead for her third album, and had told the press in July that year it was "the most pop thing, and the most electronic thing" she had made. SOPHIE handled most of the production.

Pitchfork's original 4.5 was rescored to 7.8 in 2021. Metacritic averaged 64, and the EP peaked at No. 2 on Billboard's Top Dance Albums chart. Critics at first wondered whether it was satire; Wikipedia says later reassessments decided they had been paranoid about PC Music's motives.

years.h: A. G. Cook becomes her creative director
years.p: Cook founded PC Music in London in June 2013. Charli was never formally signed to it, but his sound now runs through her records.
years.xp: The PC Music roster has included Hannah Diamond, GFOTY, [[Danny L Harle|1fd94d42-5e6a-46f2-84bf-9cc0be6c009f]] and QT, artists who often took on aliases and pitched-up vocals and treated adverts and consumer culture as material. On June 25, 2023, the label's tenth anniversary, it announced 2023 would be its final year of new releases.

years.cap: Charli xcx on stage at Glastonbury, June 2017
years.h: Fed up with the label, she makes Number 1 Angel without asking it
years.p: Ten tracks with MØ, Raye, Uffie, Abra and [[CupcakKe|43e5ae21-3048-4d4b-a274-5d3cb7ab33bd]], produced largely by Cook, SOPHIE and Danny L Harle.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says she recorded it without label permission, frustrated by conflicts and album delays. "I just got bored and made a load of songs, so I decided to put them out," she said.

Pitchfork gave it 6.3, with Katherine St. Asaph writing that it was largely stolen by its guests. Complex ranked it No. 12 on its 2017 albums list.

years.h: She directs the "Boys" video herself and casts 75 celebrities
years.p: Charli co-directs with Sarah McColgan, and the cameos include Joe Jonas, Charlie Puth, Stormzy, Diplo and Jack Antonoff.
years.xp: She said she wanted to flip the male gaze on its head. Pitchfork named it Best New Track, and it came second on year-end lists at the Guardian and NME. It was meant as the second single from a third album, but that record had leaked and was scrapped, so "Boys" came out on its own.

years.h: Pop 2 gets made in about two months in Alicia Keys' old studio
years.p: Cook produces and the guest list runs through Carly Rae Jepsen, Tove Lo, [[Caroline Polachek|d8f43dc5-4613-48ac-8c23-a62b82f8c67a]] and [[Kim Petras|54fc0558-12b5-4854-9d57-9441bcd73a72]].
years.xp:
Sessions began in September 2017, with Cook as executive producer alongside SOPHIE, Life Sim, Umru, EasyFun, King Henry and Lil Data. A planned Lil Peep collaboration was shelved after his death in November 2017. Charli hosted afterparties on [[Taylor Swift|20244d07-534f-4eff-b4d4-930878889970]]'s Reputation Stadium Tour to promote it.

Pitchfork gave it 8.4, saying it topped both Charli's and PC Music's earlier full-length work. In 2019 Pitchfork placed it 40th among the decade's best albums.

eras.title: A leaked album, then a lockdown one
eras.text: The scrapped album comes back as Charli, packed with guests. Then a pandemic hands her a bedroom studio, a Zoom link and a fan base with opinions.

years.cap: Charli xcx live at First Avenue, Minneapolis, October 11, 2019
years.h: Hackers take her demos, so she rebuilds the album as Charli
years.p: Demos left her Google Drive in 2017 and fans named the leak XCX World. The rebuild has fifteen tracks, fourteen with collaborators including [[Troye Sivan|e5712ceb-c37a-4c49-a11c-ccf4e21852d4]], Lizzo, [[Haim|aef06569-098f-4218-a577-b413944d9493]] and [[Christine and the Queens|9c90ffbf-b137-4dee-bfcc-b8010787840d]].
years.xp:
Singles were "1999" with Sivan (October 2018, No. 13 in the UK), "Blame It on Your Love" with Lizzo, "Gone" with Christine and the Queens and "White Mercedes". [[Sky Ferreira|05f3353e-e2d9-4344-a3c9-8009dd8e0427]], Clairo and Yaeji, and Haim appeared on "Cross You Out", "February 2017" and "Warm".

Pitchfork gave it 7.8. It debuted at No. 14 in the UK and No. 42 on the Billboard 200.

years.cap: Charli xcx live at First Avenue, Minneapolis
years.h: Six weeks of lockdown produce How I'm Feeling Now
years.p: She announces it on a Zoom call with fans on April 6 and releases it May 15, after fans vote on titles and artwork.
years.xp:
Executive producers were Cook, BJ Burton and Charli herself, with Dylan Brady and Danny L Harle also producing. Singles were "Forever" (April 9), "Claws" (April 23) and "I Finally Understand" (May 7).

Pitchfork gave it 7.7, and it was shortlisted for the 2020 Mercury Prize, which went to Michael Kiwanuka. "Party 4 U" went viral on TikTok in February 2025 and got a video on May 15, 2025, the album's fifth anniversary.

eras.title: SOPHIE, and the sell-out record
eras.text: The producer who rebuilt her sound dies, and Charli dedicates her next album to her. Then she goes for the big one on purpose.

years.big: "I wish I had told her more how special she was."
years.src: Crack Magazine: Charli XCX pays tribute to SOPHIE · Out: Charli XCX pays tribute to late friend SOPHIE · Wikipedia: Sophie (musician)
years.h: SOPHIE dies in Athens, aged 34
years.p: Charli's tribute, posted within days. The producer of "Vroom Vroom", "Paradise" and "Lipgloss" died on January 30, 2021, after a fall.
years.xp:
Crack Magazine reported that SOPHIE climbed up to watch the full moon and accidentally slipped and fell. Charli's post went on: "not just her music, but her as a person."

SOPHIE's 2018 album Oil of Every Pearl's Un-Insides earned a Grammy nomination for Best Dance/Electronic Album. A self-titled album, completed by her brother Benny Long, came out on September 27, 2024. Charli dedicated Crash to her and wrote "So I" for brat as a tribute.

years.cap: Charli xcx on the Crash tour, April 2022
years.src: Wikipedia: Crash (Charli XCX album) · Wikipedia: Charli XCX
years.h: She calls Crash her sell-out record, and it goes to No. 1
years.p: The last album of her Atlantic contract is a deliberate major-label play. It tops the charts in the UK, Ireland and Australia, her first UK No. 1.
years.xp:
Producers include Cook, Ariel Rechtshaid, [[George Daniel|22bb3c13-87b5-46ac-8dc9-553b6579c2e6]] of [[The 1975|5b6ebfe0-f72b-4902-bba9-74c8af0f1af0]], Justin Raisen and Oneohtrix Point Never. "New Shapes" features Christine and the Queens and Caroline Polachek, and "Beg for You" features [[Rina Sawayama|52494f9b-789d-4467-bcaf-9915e70cc8f6]]. Daniel and Charli met when she worked on No Rome's "Spinning" in 2021; they married in July 2025.

Pitchfork gave it 8.0 and called it her best full-length since Pop 2. In February 2023 she said she had signed a new deal for her next two albums, and on April 15, 2023 she played Coachella.

years.h: A Barbie song and a film score in one year
years.p: "Speed Drive" for the Barbie soundtrack enters the UK chart at No. 9, and she co-scores Bottoms with Leo Birenberg.

eras.title: brat
eras.text: Lime green, a Boiler Room and a summer named after her. She strips the sound back and the whole season adopts the word.

years.h: Boiler Room, Brooklyn: 37,000 RSVPs for 400 places
years.p: Charli plays a warehouse set called PARTYGIRL and teases new songs. Guests include Cook, Daniel, Doss, Easyfun, [[Addison Rae|610b71d9-fa78-47d6-9073-083922e73840]] and Julia Fox.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the 37,000 RSVPs were the largest in Boiler Room history, and only 400 people were let in. It was her second Boiler Room set since 2020.

years.h: "Von Dutch" opens the brat era with a Myspace throwback
years.p: Charli wrote it with Finn Keane, and the video has her dodging paparazzi through two Paris airports.
years.xp: Torso directed the video, shot at Charles de Gaulle and Le Bourget, in Terminal 2E and on display aircraft including a Boeing 747-100 and an Airbus A380. Pitchfork named it Best New Track, and it won the Grammy for Best Dance Pop Recording.

years.cap: Charli xcx on the Brat tour, BP Pulse Live, Birmingham, November 29, 2024
years.src: Wikipedia: Brat (Charli XCX album) · Wikipedia: 360 (Charli XCX song)
years.h: brat is lime green and scores 95 on Metacritic
years.p: Cook executive produces, with Keane, Cirkut and Daniel. It debuts at No. 3 on the Billboard 200 with 77,000 units.
years.xp:
The designer Brent David Freaney spent five months on the cover, Pantone 3507C. Charli said she wanted an offensive, off-trend green "to trigger the idea of something being wrong".

The "360" video, directed by Aidan Zamiri, opens with a restaurant skit where Julia Fox, Rachel Sennott, Gabbriette, Chloë Sevigny and others pick a new hot internet girl. It won Video of the Year at the UK Music Video Awards.

years.h: Three more songs, and a title that admits it
years.p: Brat and It's the Same but There's Three More Songs So It's Not arrives three days later, with "Guess" among the additions.

years.h: Brat Summer meets a presidential campaign
years.p: Charli tweets those words about Vice President Kamala Harris. The Biden-Harris campaign then takes up the album's lime-green look.
years.xp: She later clarified the tweet was not a political endorsement. On October 31, 2024, Collins English Dictionary named "brat" its word of the year.

years.h: Billie Eilish joins "Guess", and it reaches No. 1 in the UK
years.p: Wikipedia calls it Charli's first UK No. 1 as a solo artist; it also reaches No. 12 on the Hot 100.
years.xp: [[Billie Eilish|f4abc0b5-3f7a-4eff-8f78-ac078dbce533]] joined the song on August 1. The video, directed by Zamiri, came with a donation of 10,000 pairs of underwear to I Support the Girls, which supplies underwear and period products to women facing domestic violence and homelessness.

years.h: Ariana Grande, Kesha and Bon Iver rework brat
years.p: Brat and It's Completely Different but Also Still Brat also has Caroline Polachek, Tinashe, Jon Hopkins, Bladee and the 1975.
years.xp: Earlier remixes included a Cook version of "Von Dutch" with Addison Rae, "360" with [[Robyn|5a8e07d5-d932-4484-a7f7-e700793a9c94]] and Yung Lean, "Girl, so confusing" with [[Lorde|8e494408-8620-4c6a-82c2-c2ca4a1e4f12]], and "Talk talk" with Troye Sivan.

years.src: Wikipedia: Brat (Charli XCX album) · Wikipedia: List of awards and nominations received by Charli XCX
years.h: Three Grammy wins for brat, from nine nominations
years.p: Brat wins Best Dance/Electronic Album, "Von Dutch" wins Best Dance Pop Recording, and the cover wins Best Recording Package.
years.xp: Charli was also nominated for Album of the Year, and "360" for Record of the Year and Best Music Video. "Apple" was nominated for Best Pop Solo Performance and "Guess" for Best Pop Duo/Group Performance.

q: And of course, someone who none of us would be up here without, SOPHIE.
years.src: PinkNews: Charli XCX pays tribute to trans icon SOPHIE · Wikipedia: List of awards and nominations received by Charli XCX
years.h: At the Brits, she thanks SOPHIE
years.p: Charli wins British Dance Act and Best British Single for "Guess", and uses her speech to name SOPHIE.
years.xp: PinkNews reported the speech. Wikipedia's awards list credits her as the night's most awarded artist, including Album of the Year for brat.

eras.title: Music, Fashion, Film
eras.text: Emerald Fennell asks for a song and Charli writes an album. She produces a film, then makes a record about what the last two years cost.

years.cap: Charli xcx on the red carpet at the Toronto International Film Festival
years.h: The Moment premieres at Sundance, with Charli as star and producer
years.p: Zamiri directs a satire of pop stardom set in the middle of Brat Summer. Charli stars, produces through Studio365 and came up with the story.
years.xp: Charli plays a fictionalized version of herself dealing with label pressure to extend album promotion and a pretentious documentary filmmaker. A24 released it in the US. Wikipedia lists Rotten Tomatoes at 67% and Metacritic at 53, with critics calling the satire defanged. She has called it "the realest depiction of the music industry that I have ever seen".

years.h: A request for one song becomes Wuthering Heights, a whole album
years.p: Emerald Fennell asked for one song in December 2024. Charli and Keane wrote a full companion album, and it debuts at No. 1 in the UK.
years.xp:
She wrote it during the Brat Tour. Lead single "House" (November 10, 2025) has spoken-word poetry by [[John Cale|72c090b6-a68e-4cb9-b330-85278681a714]]. The album debuted at No. 8 in the US and topped the US Soundtrack Albums chart, her first US chart-topper. Metacritic gives it 82.

Sky Ferreira, who features on "Eyes of the World", later accused Charli of using her unreleased demos without credit; Charli's management denied it.

years.src: Wikipedia: Rock Music (Charli XCX song) · Wikipedia: SS26 (song)
years.h: "Rock Music" has distorted guitars, and she says it isn't rock
years.p: The lead single from the new album was recorded in October 2025 at Rue Boyer in Paris, with Cook and Keane producing.
years.xp:
Charli described the video as a video of her making a song called "rock music" that is not actually rock music. Zamiri shot it in black and white, with a TV thrown from a window and a mosh pit; Daniel cameos on drums. The Guardian gave it 4/5.

"SS26" followed on May 21 with a Torso-directed video of Charli walking Paris runways, with Carine Roitfeld, Anthony Vaccarello and Farida Khelfa appearing.

years.src: Wikipedia: Music, Fashion, Film · BroadwayWorld: Charli xcx Releases New Album · Pop Base on X: Pitchfork gives · The Needle Drop: Charli xcx - Music, Fashion, Film · Wikipedia: Charli XCX
years.h: Music, Fashion, Film runs eleven tracks and thirty minutes
years.p: Pitchfork gives it 8.2 and Best New Music. The cover, shot by Zamiri, features John Cale, Marc Jacobs and Martin Scorsese.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says it came after creative exhaustion following brat, with Fennell's invitation restarting her. The Guardian gave it five stars, calling it another gorgeously astute and disarmingly deep album about the instability of identity; Rolling Stone gave four. Pitchfork praised its little somatic thrills.

The Needle Drop's review says the closing track uses audio of David Cronenberg on mortality, and that "Magic Metal Montana" is a tribute to Cook. In June 2026 she said publicly she was in the worst place mentally she had been in her life.

years.src: Wikipedia: Charli XCX · BroadwayWorld: Charli xcx Releases New Album
years.h: The Music, Fashion, Film tour hits arenas, with Underscores opening
years.p: North America runs September 11 to October 23, including two nights each at Brooklyn's Barclays Center and the Kia Forum in Los Angeles.
years.xp: The European leg starts February 13, 2027 and finishes February 24, with Audrey Hobert opening.
